newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: ANC reveals names of spies to S.Africa truth probe.
newsitem.headline: ANC reveals names of spies to S.Africa truth probe.

text.p: South Africa's African National Congress said on Tuesday it had handed over to the country's Truth and Reconciliation Commission the names of spies within the party who had been paid by apartheid security forces.
None were in high goverment positions, the ruling party said in a statement.

Allegations surfaced earlier this year during inquiries by the Commission that up to five senior ANC members, now cabinet ministers, had spied on their own colleagues for the white regime during the war over apartheid.

Saying it was committed to transparency on the issue, the ANC added: "Reluctance to reveal these names may have the implication that such networks continue to operate for purposes that are inimical to the interests of our democracy".
"In this regard, the ANC...has submitted to the Truth and Reconciliation Commission a list of names of informers who were either apprehended or volunteered information to the movement."

The party called on the Commission, led by Nobel peace laureate and retired Anglican archbishop Desmond Tutu, to issue subpoenas compelling those former policemen who had made the allegations to provide the proof.
"The (ANC) national working committee wishes to place on record that it has no information or knowledge at its disposal of informers allegedly in high government offices," the party statement said.
President Nelson Mandela has repeatedly said he favours the naming of alleged informers, and has pledged that anyone whose actions led to deaths would be fired.
The Truth Commission was set up in 1995 to uncover as much as possible of the human rights abuses and crimes committed by all sides during apartheid.
